pack.description: Vocabulary of biology passages and talks: cells, genetics, physiology and classification.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory biology texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: a single living thing, such as an animal, a plant or a bacterium
entries.example_academic: Every organism in the pond depends, directly or indirectly, on energy from sunlight.
entries.example_spoken: It's a tiny organism, so you'll need the microscope to see it.

entries.definition: all the chemical processes in a living body that turn food into energy and new material
entries.example_academic: Small mammals have a rapid metabolism and must eat almost constantly.
entries.example_spoken: My metabolism slows down when I don't sleep enough.

entries.definition: a substance made by living cells that makes a particular chemical reaction happen faster
entries.example_academic: The enzyme breaks the long starch molecules into simple sugars.
entries.example_spoken: This detergent uses an enzyme to remove food stains.

entries.definition: a very thin layer that covers or separates parts of a cell or body
entries.example_academic: Water passes through the membrane more easily than larger molecules do.
entries.example_spoken: There's a thin membrane just under the eggshell.

entries.definition: a change in the genetic material of a living thing that can be passed on
entries.example_academic: A single mutation was enough to make the bacteria resistant to the drug.
entries.example_spoken: The white fur comes from a rare mutation.

entries.definition: the passing of physical or mental qualities from parents to their young through genes
entries.example_academic: Early studies of heredity relied on thousands of carefully bred pea plants.
entries.example_spoken: Eye color is mostly a matter of heredity.

entries.definition: a particular quality or feature of a living thing, often passed on by its parents
entries.example_academic: Traits that improve survival tend to become more common over generations.
entries.example_spoken: Stubbornness is definitely a family trait.

entries.definition: a very small living thing, such as a virus or bacterium, that causes disease
entries.example_academic: The pathogen spreads through contaminated water rather than through the air.
entries.example_spoken: Washing your hands removes most pathogens.

entries.definition: protected against a particular disease, or relating to the body's system of protection
entries.example_academic: Individuals who survived the first outbreak were immune to later infections.
entries.example_spoken: I had it as a kid, so I'm probably immune now.

entries.definition: a group of similar cells that work together to do a job in a plant or animal
entries.example_academic: Muscle tissue consumes far more energy than fat does.
entries.example_spoken: The doctor said the scar tissue will fade with time.

entries.definition: to make an exact copy of itself, or to repeat a study to see whether the result is the same
entries.example_academic: Viruses cannot replicate outside a host cell.
entries.example_spoken: Nobody has managed to replicate their results yet.

entries.definition: the young of an animal or plant, or a person's children
entries.example_academic: Parents that invest heavily in each offspring usually produce very few.
entries.example_spoken: The female protects her offspring for about two years.

entries.definition: alive but not active or growing for a period of time
entries.example_academic: The seeds remain dormant until rainfall triggers germination.
entries.example_spoken: The volcano has been dormant for centuries.

entries.definition: a substance that living things need in order to live and grow
entries.example_academic: Roots absorb nutrients that have dissolved in the surrounding water.
entries.example_spoken: Frozen vegetables keep most of their nutrients.

entries.definition: to produce and release a liquid from a cell or organ
entries.example_academic: The gland secretes a hormone that regulates blood sugar.
entries.example_spoken: Some frogs secrete a poison through their skin.

entries.definition: the process by which living things take in oxygen and use it to release energy
entries.example_academic: Cellular respiration releases the energy stored in glucose.
entries.example_spoken: The paramedic checked his pulse and respiration.

entries.definition: an animal that has a backbone
entries.example_academic: Fish were the first vertebrates to appear in the fossil record.
entries.example_spoken: Is a snake a vertebrate? Yes, it has a spine.

entries.definition: the process in which one cell divides into two cells that each have the same set of genetic material
entries.example_academic: During mitosis, each daughter cell receives an identical copy of the DNA.
entries.example_spoken: We watched mitosis happening under the microscope in lab today.

entries.definition: one of the thread-like structures in a cell that carry the genes
entries.example_academic: Humans normally have twenty-three pairs of chromosomes.
entries.example_spoken: An extra chromosome causes that condition.

entries.definition: a small part inside a cell that has a particular job
entries.example_academic: Each organelle is surrounded by its own membrane and performs a specialized task.
entries.example_spoken: The organelle that makes energy is on the exam, so learn it.

entries.definition: a protein that the body makes to find and fight a particular harmful substance
entries.example_academic: Antibodies bind to the surface of the virus and mark it for destruction.
entries.example_spoken: The blood test checks whether you have antibodies.

entries.definition: to increase very quickly in number
entries.example_academic: Once the predators had gone, the insects proliferated unchecked.
entries.example_spoken: Coffee shops have proliferated around campus.

entries.definition: the time during which a young animal develops inside its mother before birth
entries.example_academic: Elephants have a gestation period of nearly two years.
entries.example_spoken: Gestation only lasts about three weeks for mice.

entries.definition: to grow again after being lost or damaged
entries.example_academic: Some lizards can regenerate a lost tail within a few months.
entries.example_spoken: The forest regenerated faster than anyone expected.

entries.definition: describing a body part that has become small and useless during the development of a species
entries.example_academic: The whale retains vestigial hip bones inherited from land-dwelling ancestors.
entries.example_spoken: Wisdom teeth are basically vestigial.

entries.definition: the scientific system of putting living things into groups and naming them
entries.example_academic: Genetic evidence has forced biologists to revise the taxonomy of several bird families.
entries.example_spoken: The taxonomy of mushrooms is a nightmare to memorize.

entries.definition: the set of features of a living thing that you can observe, produced by its genes and its surroundings together
entries.example_academic: Identical genes can produce a different phenotype when the environment changes.
entries.example_spoken: So the phenotype is what you actually see, like height.

entries.definition: the way a living body keeps its internal conditions, such as temperature, steady
entries.example_academic: Sweating is one of the mechanisms that maintain homeostasis in mammals.
entries.example_spoken: Shivering is just your body trying to keep homeostasis.

entries.definition: a very small cell produced by fungi and some plants that can grow into a new individual
entries.example_academic: Fungal spores can survive for decades in dry soil.
entries.example_spoken: Don't shake the bag; the mold will release spores.

entries.definition: a young insect after it leaves the egg, with a body that looks very different from the adult
entries.example_academic: The larva feeds for several weeks before it forms a cocoon.
entries.example_spoken: That little worm is actually a beetle larva.
